Below Android 12 the TV can\'t tell Slightly Good TV which refresh rates it can switch to smoothly, so changing the rate may black the screen out for a second or two — sometimes more than once during a programme.\n\nWe recommend leaving Auto frame rate off here. If your TV switches cleanly, turn it on and see: you can change it back at any time.

On: ExoPlayer can also decode sound your device has no decoder for, such as DTS, TrueHD or MP2. The device\'s own decoders still come first. Off: ExoPlayer uses only the device\'s decoders. mpv always decodes with FFmpeg. Changing this restarts Slightly Good TV.
The audio decoder changes after Slightly Good TV restarts.
The Slightly Good TV icon on your TV’s home screen. The launcher may take a moment to show the change.

Opens Slightly Good TV by itself once the TV has started up, on the screen chosen in App startup. Android lets an app open by itself only when it may display over other apps, so turning this on opens that permission’s screen. Some TVs do not offer it, and then auto start cannot work there.

Opens Slightly Good TV each time the TV wakes from sleep, also when you woke it for another app. If App startup opens a channel, every wake-up starts that stream. While this is on, Slightly Good TV keeps a small background service with a silent notification. Like auto start on boot, it needs permission to display over other apps.
Stage draws Slightly Good TV’s own soft colors. Picture shows a picture of yours behind every screen. Plain is a flat dark fill.
The Slightly Good TV logo in the menu, About and setup shows its play triangle in your accent color. The icon on the home screen keeps its own colors.
Looks on GitHub for a newer Slightly Good TV now and offers to install it. Your playlists, favorites and settings stay as they are.

resources.string: Press Home or open another app while a video plays full screen or in the mini-player, and it keeps playing in a small window over the rest of the TV. Open Slightly Good TV again to bring it back full screen; close the window to stop playback. Multiview stays in Slightly Good TV.
What Slightly Good TV shows when it starts: Home, the channel you watched last, your favorites, or a channel you pick.
Dark is what Slightly Good TV is designed for. System follows the TV’s own setting where it has one; Light suits a bright room.

If a live channel has shown no picture by this time, Slightly Good TV stops trying and tells you, instead of leaving a black screen while it works through every player it has. Never keeps trying, which can take well over a minute on a channel your provider has removed. Waits your provider asks for are not counted.
Send all Slightly Good TV traffic and playback through an HTTP proxy.
This device does not allow Slightly Good TV to set exact alarms, so a recording may begin a few minutes late. Recordings start earlier to make up for it.

On any device with a browser on the same Wi-Fi — a phone, a computer or another TV — scan the QR (or open the URL), enter this PIN, choose your Slightly Good TV backup file and send it. You then pick what to restore here.
Slightly Good TV could not work out how many channels this provider allows.

Many providers never say how many channels you may watch at the same time, so Slightly Good TV finds out by opening a few and seeing which ones survive. Anything playing now will stop, and this can take up to two minutes.
Surround — send Dolby/DTS to a real 5.1/7.1 receiver. If it goes silent or stutters, Slightly Good TV still falls back to stereo and tells you.
Slightly Good TV is a player \u2014 bring your own Xtream, M3U, or Stalker source.
Slightly Good TV is a media player only. It includes no channels, playlists, or content. You are responsible for adding your own legally accessible Xtream, M3U, or Stalker sources.
